reviewedBy: Claude (Opus 5), session 57b768fe, reading the /api/capture?draft output with Jacob Kennedy
source: bookmarklet capture, 302 of 604 products (half the catalogue)
review: WARRANTY AND SERVICE REMOVED, 100 PRODUCTS. 97 products of type 'Warranty' and 3 of type 'Service' were proposed for inclusion and had been classified into the Workshop, where they would have been the LARGEST category in the room: a shelf of warranty certificates with prices on them. They are not things anybody browses for.

That was not only an include-list decision. It exposed a real bug: NONPRODUCT_TYPE in _scene.js was anchored ^...$ and tested against the whole blob (title, variant, tags and description joined), so it could only have matched a product whose entire text was the single word 'fee'. It had never fired, on any caller, since it was written. classify() now takes product_type as its own argument and 'warranty' and 'service' are in that list, so these are refused for every merchant, not just this one.

'warranty' is matched on the TYPE and deliberately NOT added to the description-reading NONPRODUCT list, because half the printers in this catalogue mention a warranty in their copy and matching the blob would have hidden real machines.

THE roomMap SENDING 3D PRINTERS TO THE AUDIO ROOM WAS DROPPED. The draft proposed {'3d printer': 'audio'} on the strength of one lowercase-typed product the classifier misread. One product does not move a category, and a 3D printer on the Audio shelf is a visible error. It falls through to workshop with the rest.

SPELLING KEPT AS THE MERCHANT WRITES IT. '3D PRINTER', 'FILAMENT' and 'Parts & Accesories' (their typo) are listed as they appear. Matching is case-insensitive so the shouting variants are redundant, but the misspelling is not, and correcting it here would silently drop those products.

HALF A CATALOGUE. 302 of 604 captured. The include list is drawn from 25 product types across that half and is the conservative direction to be wrong in: a type that appears only in the unread half will be dropped rather than published unseen. Worth a second capture before assuming the Workshop is complete.
Prices run from 1 dollar to 62,895. The top end is industrial CNC, which is real, but this merchant will own every price-descending sort on the site.
